# Limitations

The primary sparse-relay claim is scoped to Gemma 3 270M, one dictionary and
task, and lexical rather than semantic outcomes. Gemma 3 1B supplies an
exploratory sparse steerability audit, a stochastic hybrid result for one
mediator-valid feature, and a matched natural-state-derived residual
replication; it does not establish a broad sparse transmission phenotype.
Greedy results are supplemented by exact
two-article stochastic mixtures, not unrestricted vocabulary sampling. S1 was
attribution-selected and amplified by up to \(5\times\), so we decompose
this handle rather than a unique ontology; large gain may be off-manifold.
S2 often derails; the L5/F383 localization is exploratory and post-selection
on the evaluation prompts, may encode a vowel class, and has only four
matched controls (\(p=0.20\)). S1's leftover overlaps its random control;
the switched subset is descriptive; the twin estimate is small-\(N\); and
TV is nonadditive.

The synthetic pair validates estimand polarity, not transformer behavior.
The pre-article patch establishes sensitivity on 12 held-out pairs but is
target-constructed, vocabulary-cued, a full residual transplant, and
subthreshold: private-route capacity, not a sparse plan. All 12 pairs are
consonant-native, so inserted `an` is mismatched for both alternatives.
Layer selection uses four development pairs. The interaction shows
article-prefix compatibility, not a meaningful allocation trade-off.
Model-family, task, sampling, and prompt-controlled route allocation remain
open. The effect-matched 1B coalition uses 24 features at \(20\times\), often
pushes `a/an` below other tokens, and therefore exits the mediator support of
the binary article assay. The constrained one-feature frontier preserves that
support and has a measurable stochastic public component, but its effect is
low-amplitude and comes from a single feature selected on development prompts.
A representative full-active-graph audit makes simple node
truncation unlikely, but the 1B CLT reconstruction audit is uneven across
layers and has a substantial affine skip; sparse-selection failure therefore
cannot be assigned uniquely to model scale or model organization.

The float32 audit casts only the final normalization and unembedding; it
does not rerun the transformer or CLT in float32. Natural-state-derived residual patches
are full-state transplants selected at one pooled development layer. They
show private target influence but no article change, so they do not
establish causal allocation or a public/private regime switch. The two
32-feature attribution calibrations have resolution for moderate monotone
effects, not proof of zero association; their bootstrap intervals are wide for
downstream outcomes, their intervention gain remains \(5\times\), and the 1B
original channel analysis used an outcome-dependent all-prompt gate. Our
matched signed reanalysis avoids that gate, but still has only 32 feature-level
observations per scale. The gain-law identity is algebraic; its empirical value
depends on how accurately local margin movement can be predicted before the
intervention is run. Two-way holdout is strong at 270M, but the 1B
attribution-based cross-validation remains weak, and `a/an` supplies little
variation in branch leverage. General predictive leverage requires another
mediator task.

The released `is/are` subtraction task supplies a second mediator but not a
positive generality result: both pretrained models are behaviorally poor on the
arithmetic content, and the target-derived patches fail local target efficacy.
This rules out using these runs to test mediator information capacity; it does
not show that `is/are` cannot externalize causal state in a model that solves the
task. Testing such a model without exceeding the present local hardware remains
open.

**Ethics.** This public-model study uses synthetic prompts and no human or
personal data. We mitigate overclaiming through scoped conclusions and
released code/results. AI-agent assistance is declared in the NeurIPS
checklist.
